items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: There’s another jazz society in the Fort Lauderdale area called the Gold Coast Jazz Society that used to be booked by a very capable woman named Lee Amley who has since passed away.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well it probably will be a good one with Dick Hyman.

Yeah. It’s an interesting little thing. We have a repertory orchestra. There’s another jazz society in the Fort Lauderdale area called the Gold Coast Jazz Society that used to be booked by a very capable woman named Lee Amley who has since passed away. And their board is a board. They can’t seem to decide what their actual thrust is, whether it’s music or — well I haven’t been that — I used to advise them on some things, but I’ve been too busy on this other one now. Anyway we’re doing a concert over there with…

do that with him and they do a trumpet feature that Chris LaBarbara, a very excellent trumpet player over there, he’s like Mister Repertory, he can imitate anybody. I mean he can do Harry James, he can do Louis, and he can do Roy Eldridge very well, and you name it. And it’s an interesting thing. So then we add Dick in there, Dick comes out and does all his little stride things, the Jelly Rollisms, and I mean Dick is the living embodiment of the Encyclopedia of Jazz at his fingertips.
